quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Addition
quests.contextSentence: She packed her laptop, her charger, ___ a notebook before the conference.
quests.completedSentence: She packed her laptop, her charger, and a notebook before the conference.
quests.ruleExplanation: All three items belong on the same list of things she's bringing, so 'and' simply adds the last one.
quests.nativeTip: Think about whether these three items are all going into the same bag.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Addition
quests.contextSentence: My neighbor waters his plants every morning ___ walks his dog right after.
quests.completedSentence: My neighbor waters his plants every morning and walks his dog right after.
quests.ruleExplanation: Nothing here contrasts or depends on anything else — 'and' just links two routine actions together.
quests.nativeTip: Both actions are simply part of the same morning routine.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Addition
quests.contextSentence: The new phone case is thin, lightweight, ___ surprisingly durable.
quests.completedSentence: The new phone case is thin, lightweight, and surprisingly durable.
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence is building a list of good qualities, and 'and' joins the final one to the rest.
quests.nativeTip: These are three separate qualities being listed about the same case.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Contrast
quests.contextSentence: The meeting ran long, ___ everyone stayed focused until the end.
quests.completedSentence: The meeting ran long, but everyone stayed focused until the end.
quests.ruleExplanation: You'd expect people to tune out during a long meeting, but they didn't — that unexpected turn is a contrast.
quests.nativeTip: A long meeting usually causes people to lose focus — did that happen here?

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Contrast
quests.contextSentence: The jacket looked expensive, ___ it was actually on sale.
quests.completedSentence: The jacket looked expensive, but it was actually on sale.
quests.ruleExplanation: The jacket's expensive look clashes with its actual low price, and 'but' signals that mismatch.
quests.nativeTip: Its appearance pointed to one price; the real price was a different story.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Contrast
quests.contextSentence: We arrived at the airport early, ___ our flight was delayed by two hours anyway.
quests.completedSentence: We arrived at the airport early, but our flight was delayed by two hours anyway.
quests.ruleExplanation: Being early made no difference in the end, and 'but' points out that ironic contrast.
quests.nativeTip: Arriving early should have meant less waiting — did it work out that way?

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Choice
quests.contextSentence: Would you like your coffee hot ___ iced?
quests.completedSentence: Would you like your coffee hot or iced?
quests.ruleExplanation: Only one option gets chosen here, and 'or' is exactly how you offer two alternatives.
quests.nativeTip: The customer will end up with just one of these two.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Choice
quests.contextSentence: You can send the report today ___ wait until the morning meeting.
quests.completedSentence: You can send the report today or wait until the morning meeting.
quests.ruleExplanation: Two separate options are being laid out for the reader to pick between, which is exactly what 'or' does.
quests.nativeTip: These are two possible paths, and the person will take one of them.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Choice
quests.contextSentence: Tap the blue icon ___ swipe left to see more options.
quests.completedSentence: Tap the blue icon or swipe left to see more options.
quests.ruleExplanation: The instructions describe two separate methods for the same goal, so 'or' shows they're alternatives, not steps to do together.
quests.nativeTip: These are two different ways to reach the same result — you'd only need one.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: The wind picked up suddenly, ___ we packed up the picnic early.
quests.completedSentence: The wind picked up suddenly, so we packed up the picnic early.
quests.ruleExplanation: The sudden wind is the cause, and packing up is what followed from it, which is the pattern 'so' introduces.
quests.nativeTip: The wind is the cause — what did it lead the group to do?

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: Rent went up again this year, ___ I started looking for a cheaper apartment.
quests.completedSentence: Rent went up again this year, so I started looking for a cheaper apartment.
quests.ruleExplanation: The rent increase is what drove the search for a cheaper place, so 'so' marks that cause-and-effect link.
quests.nativeTip: The rising rent pushed the speaker toward a new decision.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: My back was hurting all week, ___ I booked an appointment with a physiotherapist.
quests.completedSentence: My back was hurting all week, so I booked an appointment with a physiotherapist.
quests.ruleExplanation: Booking the appointment happened because of the back pain, and 'so' introduces that outcome.
quests.nativeTip: The pain is what pushed the speaker to take action.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The workshop was postponed ___ the guest speaker came down with the flu.
quests.completedSentence: The workshop was postponed because the guest speaker came down with the flu.
quests.ruleExplanation: The speaker's illness is the reason the workshop got postponed, which is exactly what 'because' introduces.
quests.nativeTip: The illness is the explanation behind the schedule change.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: He rewrote the whole essay ___ his laptop crashed before he could save it.
quests.completedSentence: He rewrote the whole essay because his laptop crashed before he could save it.
quests.ruleExplanation: The laptop crash is the reason all that rewriting was necessary, so 'because' fits here.
quests.nativeTip: Something went wrong first, and that's what forced the extra work.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The coach benched two players ___ they missed practice all week.
quests.completedSentence: The coach benched two players because they missed practice all week.
quests.ruleExplanation: Missing practice is the reason behind the benching, and 'because' explains that link.
quests.nativeTip: Their absence from practice is what led to the coach's decision.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: The app sends a notification ___ your package leaves the warehouse.
quests.completedSentence: The app sends a notification when your package leaves the warehouse.
quests.ruleExplanation: The notification fires at the specific moment the package leaves, and 'when' marks that exact point in time.
quests.nativeTip: The alert is tied to one exact moment in the delivery process.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: Call me ___ you land at the airport.
quests.completedSentence: Call me when you land at the airport.
quests.ruleExplanation: Landing is the trigger moment for the call, so 'when' is used to point to that exact time.
quests.nativeTip: The call should happen right at the moment of landing, not earlier.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: Everyone applauded ___ the new manager announced the bonus.
quests.completedSentence: Everyone applauded when the new manager announced the bonus.
quests.ruleExplanation: The clapping starts right at the moment of the announcement, which is what 'when' signals.
quests.nativeTip: The applause broke out at the exact instant of the announcement.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: Check the departure board ___ you head to the gate.
quests.completedSentence: Check the departure board before you head to the gate.
quests.ruleExplanation: Checking the board needs to happen first so the gate information is correct, and 'before' places it ahead of the other action.
quests.nativeTip: One action should come earlier, so the other one is based on accurate information.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: Let the pan heat up ___ you add the oil.
quests.completedSentence: Let the pan heat up before you add the oil.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pan needs time to heat first, and 'before' shows that the oil goes in only after that earlier step.
quests.nativeTip: One step needs a head start, so the next step goes in properly.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: Please review the contract carefully ___ you sign it.
quests.completedSentence: Please review the contract carefully before you sign it.
quests.ruleExplanation: The review has to come earlier than the signature, and 'before' sets up that required order.
quests.nativeTip: Reading needs to happen first, so the signature comes with full understanding.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: She stretches for ten minutes ___ every run.
quests.completedSentence: She stretches for ten minutes after every run.
quests.ruleExplanation: The stretching happens once the run is finished, so 'after' places it in that later position.
quests.nativeTip: The stretching is a cool-down, not a warm-up.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: The store restocked its shelves ___ the holiday rush finally ended.
quests.completedSentence: The store restocked its shelves after the holiday rush finally ended.
quests.ruleExplanation: The restocking only happened once the entire rush was over, which is the later-time meaning of 'after'.
quests.nativeTip: The busy period had to fully pass before the new stock could go out.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: We usually watch a movie together ___ dinner is finished.
quests.completedSentence: We usually watch a movie together after dinner is finished.
quests.ruleExplanation: Dinner comes first and the movie follows, so 'after' marks the movie as the later event.
quests.nativeTip: The movie is the second part of the evening, not the first.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: She answered emails ___ she waited for the meeting to start.
quests.completedSentence: She answered emails while she waited for the meeting to start.
quests.ruleExplanation: Answering emails and waiting were happening at the same time, and 'while' links two ongoing actions like that.
quests.nativeTip: Both things were happening together during the same stretch of time.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: He hums along to the radio ___ he washes the dishes.
quests.completedSentence: He hums along to the radio while he washes the dishes.
quests.ruleExplanation: Humming and washing dishes overlap in time rather than one following the other, which is what 'while' expresses.
quests.nativeTip: Both activities are happening at once, side by side.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: Many commuters read on their phones ___ they ride the subway.
quests.completedSentence: Many commuters read on their phones while they ride the subway.
quests.ruleExplanation: The reading takes place during the ride, at the same time, which 'while' is built to describe.
quests.nativeTip: The reading fills the same time as the ride itself, not before or after it.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: The design team kept revising the logo ___ the client finally approved it.
quests.completedSentence: The design team kept revising the logo until the client finally approved it.
quests.ruleExplanation: The revisions kept going up to the moment of approval, and 'until' marks that ending point of a continuing action.
quests.nativeTip: The revising continued right up to one final stopping point.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: Keep icing the sprain ___ the swelling goes down.
quests.completedSentence: Keep icing the sprain until the swelling goes down.
quests.ruleExplanation: Icing is meant to continue up to the point where the swelling disappears, which is the stopping point 'until' introduces.
quests.nativeTip: The icing should continue right up to the point when the swelling stops.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: Keep your receipt ___ the return period ends.
quests.completedSentence: Keep your receipt until the return period ends.
quests.ruleExplanation: The receipt needs to be kept up to the closing date of the return window, which is the endpoint meaning of 'until'.
quests.nativeTip: The receipt stays useful right up to one final cutoff.
